subject: Aurora SLO handshake & customer-led stress run logistics
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurorahealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: SLOs, ramp, and next steps for customer-led run

Hi Priya / Samir — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-led stress run scheduled this month. Short bullets and asks below.

Summary of what we agreed on call:
- Primary SLOs to validate: 95th pct P99 token latency below 250ms for non-streaming gen; 95th pct streaming event latency < 300ms (server-to-client); 99th pct tail target for both <= 500ms.
- Throughput target: sustained ~3,500 inference requests/min during plateau; peak bursts up to 7k rpm for 10m.
- Concurrency: simulated concurrency goal for standard requests = 500 concurrent sessions; streaming/ws connections target = 200 concurrent clients.
- Workloads: mixed small prompts (<=128 tokens) and medium prompts (<=1024 tokens); one long prompt trace for KV cache validation.

Immediate asks from Aurora to proceed:
1) Final test window preference (2–4 hour windows, Pacific TZ). Please confirm a 2-hour and an alternate 4-hour slot.
2) IPs to allowlist (we will provide egress IPs; you should provide inbound test client IPs for outbound webhook callbacks).
3) Do you want us to run the k6 runner or do you prefer to run Locust from your infra? We can provide both scripts.
4) Identify the QA contact who will accept test credentials and handle signing off on functional sanity.

What Redwood will provide before the run:
- k6 scenario bundle (attached) with the ramp profile we discussed and an alternative stress profile.
- a short readme with test account credentials + token expiry/rotation notes (attached).
- an allowlist file for your security team with egress IPs (attached).
- an internal runbook and escalation contacts (we will share a Drive link).

Suggested ramp profile (we proposed on call):
- 15m warmup to 25% traffic, 30m linear ramp to plateau, 60m plateau, 10m ramp-down. Burst tests at minute 40 and minute 80 with 2–3x baseline.

If that all looks good I'll open the HubSpot deal activity and provision a short-lived test account for your QA. Can you confirm test window options and the QA point-of-contact?

Thanks — Tessa
--
Tessa Morgan
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
(t) +1-415-555-0182
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurorahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>, QA Team <qa@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLOs, ramp, and next steps for customer-led run

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming:
- Preferred window: Tue Apr 20 09:00–11:00 PT. Alternate: Thu Apr 22 13:00–17:00 PT (we can take the 4-hour slot if needed).
- IPs for our test agents: 198.51.100.12, 198.51.100.13, 198.51.100.14 (these are the egress addresses from our load generators).
- We will run Locust from our k8s cluster; please send the k6 as a reference and the Locust scenarios if you have them.
- QA primary: Samir Patel (samir.patel@aurorahealth.com) and CC to qa@aurorahealth.com.

One question: for streaming scenarios (websocket), can you confirm whether the service will accept persistent connections from our agents behind NAT (we will exercise 200 concurrent ws clients from single node)? Also, are you able to return incremental tokens at the same latency targets or should we expect higher variance for streaming?

PRIYA
Priya Shah
Principal PM, Integrations | Aurora Health Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLOs, ramp, and next steps for customer-led run

Looping in infra — Connor / Marcus, we'll need to provision a short-lived test API key scoped to AURO-2371 and enable a "test" routing group that uses cached models and a dedicated burst lane. Please note the token will expire after 48h unless Aurora requests an extension.

Connor — can you prepare:
- a test API key + instructions (token rotation guidance)
- a short WebSocket endpoint URL for streaming tests (wss://stream-test-us.redwood.ai/aurora)
- a reportable metric set (latency, token/sec, kv-cache hit-rate) exposed to their team via a temporary dashboard link.

I'll attach the allowlist for our egress and the k6 tarball to this thread (attached by Tessa). Marcus, please confirm we include the streaming socket tuning flags (max concurrent connections = 250, per-connection send buffer limits set low to avoid head-of-line blocking).

Karthik
VP, Production Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@aurorahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLOs, ramp, and next steps for customer-led run

Thanks — confirms on windows and IPs. A couple quick items from our ops side:
- Ramp profile: we'll tweak the plateau length to 90m if you prefer that for persistence testing.
- For streaming: we'll run 200 concurrent ws clients distributed across 4 nodes (approx 50 per node). We'll validate reconnect behavior and partial message delivery.
- Ramp behavior: can you confirm your k6/locust script supports per-user randomized think times and also the ability to pin a small % (5–10%) of long-running sessions to exercise KV cache across tokens?

Also, do you have a template for the post-run summary that includes latency percentiles, error breakdown by route, and token counts? If you can drop the template in the Drive link we will use it to sign-off.

Samir
Samir Patel
Engineering Manager, QA Automation | Aurora Health Systems
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@aurorahealth.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLOs, ramp, and next steps for customer-led run

Perfect — thanks for the confirmations and details. Quick commitments from our side: 
- We will provide the Locust scenarios (converted from k6) and a short how-to run doc by EOD today. Attachment: aurora_k6_scenarios.tar.gz includes both k6 and converted locust scripts.
- Connor will provision the test API key and the streaming wss endpoint; token guidance included in aurora_test_account_readme.md.
- Drive folder now populated with the post-run summary template and the runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example/aurora-loadtest (shared).
- We will set the default plateau to 60m but are ok with a 90m plateau if Aurora prefers — please confirm final plateau length in your run plan.

Next steps:
- Aurora to confirm final plateau length and confirm the 20 Apr 09:00–11:00 PT slot OR choose the alternate Thu 22 Apr 13:00–17:00 PT.
- Aurora ops to confirm they can accept 200 concurrent WS connections from NATted agents (Samir has indicated yes).
- Redwood to publish the temporary dashboard link and provision keys by EOD tomorrow (Karthik / Connor).

If all good, I'll mark the HubSpot activity as "run scheduled" and add the run-time contacts.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to it.

--
